slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies of people who are
quietly brilliant

learning dead languages

learn twenty words of latin or ancient greek. you'll start recognising their roots everywhere, and your own language will suddenly make much more sense.

reading the footnotes

read the footnotes and sources in your next non fiction book. that's where the most interesting arguments hide, and most readers skip them completely.

a lesson a day

spend 5 minutes a day on a new subject: astronomy, art history, economics. small daily lessons add up to a curious mind that can talk about almost anything.

slides.texte_overlay:
solving riddles

solve one logic riddle with your morning coffee. riddles train you to question your first answer, which is the most important habit of any brilliant mind.

visiting small museums

visit small local museums instead of only the famous ones. fewer crowds mean more time with every object, and strange local stories nobody else knows.
